newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates Friends Provident Life Office A plus.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Friends Provident Life Office A plus.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Monday it assigned its A plus financial strength rating to Friends Provident Life Office (FP).
At the same time, S&P said it assigned its A minus long-term rating to FP Finance Plc's 200 million stg perpetual subordinated debt issue, which is guaranteed by its parent FP.
"The notes will be subordinated such that they are admissible towards the statutory capital base of FP," S&P said in a statement.

"The ratings are based on FP's diversified business portfolio, good operating performance including excellent persistency and systems, and very good capitalisation," S&P said. "However, investment performance has recently lagged peers and FP operates in a very competitive market where it lacks the scale of market leaders."
S&P said it expected recent restructuring, IT investments and increased sales volumes to reduce expense levels and further improve customer service.

"This will help to maintain market position but S&P believes both improved investment performance and possibly an acquisition to increase critical mass would be required to propel FP into the top tier of UK life companies," the agency said.
S&P listed the following major rating factors.
- Friends Provident has a diversified business position with a wide range of products and an increasingly varied distribution base.
- Operating performance is good. S&P said the pressure on costs was likely to remain as competition and disclosure of commissions squeezed profit margins on many products.
- Policy persistency is the best in the UK life market.
- Capitalisation is very good although the published solvency ratios appear low in comparison with peers in view of FP's conservative assessment of liabilties.
- Financial flexibility is believed by S&P to be good notwithstanding FP's mutual status.
- Investment performance has lagged peers recently due to under-performance in the UK equity and property markets.

- FP aims to increase its market position but S&P believes this may be difficult to achieve with competition coming from both market leaders enjoying significant scale economies and from smaller niche and low cost players.
